newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose sharply against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Thursday in quiet trading, dealers said.
On Wednesday, there was no trading in foreign currency due to the New Year holiday.

"The business sector was waiting until the end of the year before it started converting dollars into shekels," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim. "Israeli companies that made overseas issues also have to change their foreign currency into shekels now."
The official basket rate fell to 6.5 percent under the diagonal rate, he noted.

The shekel can fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2420 shekels against 3.2510 shekels on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6285 shekels against 3.6354 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8004 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8031 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.0961 shekels against 2.0974 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2400 shekels.
